title: There Is a World We Have Not Seen
description: There Is a World We Have Not Seen in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 450, “The Spiritual World”, where the book credits them to Briggs' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: There is a world we have not seen, That time can ne'er de-stroy, Where mor-tal foot-step hath not been, Nor ear hath heard its joy.

lines: There is a world we have not seen,
Where mortal footstep hath not been,
Nor ear hath heard its joy.
There is a world, — and O how blest!
And never did an angel guest
And this pure world is ever bright
Flow round it from the throne.
Look not abroad with roving mind
It comes, where'er the lowly find

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
